newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serb leader agrees Moslem residents can return.
newsitem.headline: Serb leader agrees Moslem residents can return.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic agreed on Wednesday that pre-war Moslem residents should not be prevented from resettling a village now on the Serb side of Bosnia's ethnic boundary line.

Plavsic, a hardline nationalist, made the statement after meeting international peace coordinator Carl Bildt for the second time in three days after a Serb mob attack on Moslems preparing to move back into the hamlet of Gajevi.

"We will accept people who wish to return but on condition they had houses in that area earlier," Plavsic said after the talks with Bildt, the commander of the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia and an international police official.
"All of this of course should be with the necessary documentation and proof and with respect of agreed procedure."

Bildt, international High Representative to Bosnia, earlier this week reprimanded the Bosnian Serb leadership over violence against non-Serb refugees seeking to regain homes in accordance with the 1995 Dayton peace treaty on Bosnia.
The Bosnian Serb Republic covers half of Bosnia but is not a separate state under terms of the treaty.
Under the Dayton peace accord refugees from all three sides are allowed to return to their homes but the process, fraught with lingering ethnic mistrust, has barely begun.
